classification.difficultyReason: Parts a and b are chained Pythagoras steps in exact surd form with the diagram supplied, so each is routine. The hardest demand is part c. The student must see that the squared hypotenuse rises by 1 each time, generalise to sqrt(n+1), and apply it at n = 24. Parts a and b scaffold this pattern, and the generalisation is explicit. That makes it harder than the single-step integer-triad check in p14-q6. It is easier than p34-q4, which needs several derived sides, an equal-sides inference and an arc perimeter. It is far below p37-q11, which has no scaffolded parts.

content.prompt: Right-angled triangles are joined as shown. Answer in exact form.

children.label: c
children.prompt: The pattern continues. Find the length of the hypotenuse of the 24th triangle.

answer.worked:
The hypotenuses are $\sqrt{2},\sqrt{3},\sqrt{4},\sqrt{5},\dots$ Each squared hypotenuse is $1$ more than the last, so the $n$th triangle has hypotenuse $\sqrt{n+1}$.
$$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{24+1}\\h&=\sqrt{25}\\h&=5\end{align*}$$
